Device Trust Scoring

A security metric that evaluates the trustworthiness of a device based on hardware, software, configuration, compliance posture, and real-time risk signals to inform access decisions.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Device Trust Scoring?

In this glossary, Device Trust Scoring refers to: A security metric that evaluates the trustworthiness of a device based on hardware, software, configuration, compliance posture, and real-time risk signals to inform access decisions.

How is Device Trust Scoring used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Use device trust scoring to automatically restrict access for devices that fail security compliance or exhibit high-risk behavior patterns."

Why does Device Trust Scoring matter in cybersecurity?

Device Trust Scoring matters because it supports clear communication in Cloud contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Who uses Device Trust Scoring?

Device Trust Scoring is mainly used by SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders.

What category does Device Trust Scoring belong to?

In this glossary, Device Trust Scoring is grouped under Cloud. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.
